Sam — thanks for the clear requirements. I sketched an initial throughput/latency model based on our Redwood-verified M1 and M2 family performance and their typical prompt vs. generation token mix. High level assumptions (attached spreadsheet has line-by-line math):

- Target SLO: 95th <= 300ms for 256-token generation (end-to-end: request ingress -> first token out latency + tail).
- Model candidates: rwl-7b (quantized int8), rwl-13b-q4, rwl-70b-8bit. Baseline perf (single GPU warm, prompt cached):
  - rwl-7b: ~1200 tokens/sec per GPU (generation), median latency per 256-gen ≈ 213ms; 95th ≈ 280ms with 1.2x variance.
  - rwl-13b-q4: ~700 tokens/sec per GPU, median 365ms (so fails 95th target unless batching aggressive).
  - rwl-70b-8bit: ~200 tokens/sec per GPU, median 1.2s (not feasible for 300ms SLO).

- Workload mix: 70% short (<=64 tokens), 30% long (>=512). Effective tokens/sec demand at peak estimated at 75k tokens/sec across users using per-request average tokens (prompt + gen).

Sizing options we recommend:
A) Performance-first (guaranteed SLO): Reserve 12 M1 GPUs (rwl-7b optimized path) with smart prefix caching + continuous batching. Provides ~14k tokens/sec usable headroom (sustained) and estimated 95th latency margin ~15%. Expected cost: $X/month (see attachment).
B) Cost-balanced (some SLO trade): 8 M1 GPUs + fallback to rwl-13b for non-critical routes, API-level routing policy to send high-priority requests to dedicated pool. Headroom smaller (~20% at peak), 95th at ~290-360ms depending on sequence length.
C) Scale-on-demand burst: Small base of 6 GPUs reserved + autoscale when queue depth > threshold; relies on warm pools in same AZs to hit 300ms for short requests but longer warm-up risk for long-form.

Key levers to hit 300ms at 95th: enforce max gen length for SLA-bound routes (<=256), use prefix caching for repeated prompts, and prefer rwl-7b quantized on dedicated. Also recommend a canary with 2-week simulated load test to validate the 95th percentile under real concurrency.

I've attached a sizing spreadsheet (pegasus_dedicated_sizing_v1.xlsx) and a short SLA playbook (pegasus_sla_playbook.pdf) with rollout recommendations.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Quick commercial + ops readout: per review with infra finance and Dedicated ops, Option A (12 M1 GPUs, rwl-7b quantized path) is the only configuration that meets the 95th<=300ms target with at least 25% headroom across your stated mix. Key notes:

- Sizing math (summary): 12 GPUs * 1200 tokens/sec ≈ 14.4k tokens/sec usable. With batching + caching efficiency assumed at 1.9x effective improvement (realistic for Pegasus prompt patterns), effective throughput ~27k tokens/sec. We mapped to request-level concurrency and observed that our model of end-to-end 95th remains ~260-285ms under the simulated client mix. See tab 'latency-model' in attached spreadsheet.
- Cost: Pilot list price for 12 GPUs reserved for 6 months = $138,000 (one-time commitment invoice applied monthly). Includes one simulated load test and 5 days of Dedicated ops runbook support. Discounts and SLA add-ons can be negotiated; draft line item for 20% pilot discount provided in attachment.
- Runbook & timeline: We can provision a warm pool in us-west-2 and run the simulated 2-week soak/test starting Jan 24. Deliverables: test report, 95/99 latency curves, parameter tuning, and final commit recommendation by Feb 10.
- Contract notes: We'll include fallback routing policies and a short-term credit if 95th exceeds target during the first 30 days while we tune.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Sam: confirm go-ahead for Option A pilot pricing and Jan 24 test window.
2) Redwood: prepare pilot MSA draft for Pegasus legal review (Neha will own).
3) Infra: schedule Dedicated provisioning + baseline telemetry dashboards (Marissa).

Markus Klein
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference
